name: Certified Information Security Manager

fee.note: US$575 for ISACA members (membership is a separate purchase). Certification adds a one-time US$50 application fee after passing, then a yearly maintenance fee of US$45 (members) or US$85 (non-members).

exam.format: 150 multiple-choice questions in 4 hours, at a PSI test centre or remotely proctored, in English, Chinese, Spanish, Japanese, French or German. Registration opens a six-month window to sit the exam. Scores are scaled; pretest items are not scored.

scope: Managing an enterprise information security program: governance and strategy, risk management, program development and management, and incident readiness and response.
requirements: Anyone can sit the exam. To be certified: five or more years of CISM work experience across at least three of the four domains, gained within the 10 years before applying and verified by a supervisor; ISACA's candidate guide allows waivers for up to two of those years. Apply within five years of passing, pay the US$50 application fee and follow ISACA's Code of Professional Ethics and CPE policy.
ai_policy: Check the current assessment rules. AI-assisted study does not imply permission during the exam.
caveats: The exam moved to a new content outline on 3 November 2026: more emphasis on security strategy and program development, plus enterprise architecture and information security architecture. The weights here are the new ones. ISACA released updated prep material on 1 September 2026; material written for the 2022 outline predates the new content areas.

Validity is yearly: ISACA renews the certification each calendar year with the maintenance fee and at least 20 CPE hours, and 120 over each three-year cycle. From 1 January 2027 at least 90 of those 120 hours must align with the exam content outline.
Up to four attempts in a rolling 12 months (waits of 30, 90 and 90 days), each paid in full.

discounts.text: ISACA members pay US$575 for the exam instead of US$760.

access.retake: Up to four attempts in a rolling 12 months: wait 30 days before the second attempt and 90 days before the third and the fourth. Each attempt is paid in full.

timeline.text: The updated CISM exam is in use: same four domains and weights, more on security strategy and program development, and new enterprise and information security architecture content.
New CPE rule: at least 90 of the 120 CPE hours in each three-year cycle must align with the CISM exam content outline.

domains_note: Weights from ISACA's CISM exam content outline, in force since 3 November 2026 and repeated in ISACA's 10 September 2026 announcement and its 2026 candidate guide; read 2026-11-17.
